standard_prerequisites.name: Fitting-type ideals I_i(M^bullet, f) of a bounded complex of finite free modules
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: the notation I_i in the statement at source lines 28016-28017
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the two ideals being compared and the augmented maps whose minors generate them.

standard_prerequisites.name: Base change of a complex of finite free modules and of the minors of a matrix
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the generators of the two ideals term by term, which is the whole content of the proof.

core_obligations: Recall the definition of I_i(M^bullet, f) as generated by the i-th minors of the augmented map (f, d^i) : M^i -> M^i oplus M^{i+1} in the given complex (proof lines 28020-28022).

Base change the complex and the element f to B, obtaining the element g and the complex of finite free B-modules M^bullet tensor_A B with augmented maps (g, d^i) (statement line 28015-28016, proof line 28023).

Observe that the minors of (f, d^i) map to the corresponding minors of (g, d^i) under A -> B, since both the entries of the matrices and the minors are polynomial in those entries (proof lines 28021-28023).
Conclude the ideal equality I_i(M^bullet, f)B = I_i(M^bullet tensor_A B, g) from that term-by-term correspondence of generators (proof lines 28020-28023).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring map A -> B, a nonzerodivisor f in A, a bounded complex M^bullet of finite free A-modules, and assumes that f maps to a nonzerodivisor g in B; the conclusion is the equality I_i(M^bullet, f)B = I_i(M^bullet tensor_A B, g) of ideals (source lines 28012-28018). The proof has to compare the i-th minors of two different maps: the map (f, d^i) : M^i -> M^i oplus M^{i+1} attached to the complex over A, and the corresponding map (g, d^i) after base change to B (proof lines 28020-28023). What makes the statement non-formal is that the ideal I_i is generated by the minors of an augmented map rather than of the differential alone, so the equality is not immediate from base change of a matrix; the author states the whole argument as the single observation that those minors map to those minors.
